title: Black Benny's funeral and character
summary: He describes Benny's killing, his huge funeral with several bands and his bass drum on the hearse, and his reputation as a protector.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: In the third ward and, uh, well that was the end of him. And I've never seen a funeral in my life like he had. I think they had about three or four bands. Really? Yeah. And on top of the hoist, well that's before they started using these limousines. They were using horses at that time. And on top of the hoist, they had his bass drum up there. His real drum. His real bass drum. Yeah, his real bass drum. And they had it up on top of the hoist. And I'll never forget it. I saw him at Canal and Claiborne. We was turning Canal into Claiborne going into the St. Louis St. Cemetery. Well he's buried over there. Yeah, he's buried in one of them cemeteries there. I didn't have time to see which one it was because I was going to work at the time, you know? And that's where they buried him out there in one of them cemeteries. No, Mr. He's out there?
No. I think it's back in Gentilly. Mount Olivet I believe.

Oh yes, that's where Stella stands. Yeah, Mount Olivet I think he's buried. I think they're taking him as far as Biennival and Galvis. And that's where the bands left the funeral. Take him on out there. But that's where they had his bass drum. I've never seen a funeral for no musician like that since. Trumpet, flares, trombone, flares, and nobody else. They really honored him. They really honored him a great deal.
Oh, he was a popular man. And what the people liked about him, he was what you say a protector. If he was with you and somebody wanted to make a little trouble for you, he was right there with you.
That's what Armstrong says too. He may have been a little bit tough, but he helped me out and keep you out. Yeah, he was right there with you. And he didn't take nothing off of nobody.
Not off of anybody, not off the policemen. And the police in them days was men alongside what we have today.

We got mostly youngsters now dead, but when I was a kid coming up, you had policemen way up in their age that had been on the force for years. And they knew how to treat people. But black men didn't worry about nobody. And then he just had to go get killed by that woman. He got killed by her and somebody killed her. Well that was that.
